publication.title: Iraq helicopter proposal: reported U.S. approval does not establish a completed sale
publication.summary: Reports trace the August 31 decision to a State Department notification for a possible $800 million Bell helicopter package. The original page was identified but could not be retrieved directly; an accessible reproduction is linked. Aircraft quantities, final contract terms and delivery remain unverified.
publication.body:
The reported August 31 decision concerns a possible $800 million foreign military sale to Iraq, including Bell 412EPX and Bell 407M helicopters and related equipment and support. It does not establish a completed purchase or delivery.

The source trail is now clearer. Military Times links the State Department notification, while Deagel reproduces its text. Both identify Bell Textron as the principal contractor. This review could not retrieve the official page directly because it returned HTTP 403. The accessible accounts therefore strengthen the traceability of the original report without becoming multiple independent confirmations of implementation.

The reviewed notification gives no aircraft quantities. Earlier Iraqi acquisition plans must not be substituted for missing quantities in this proposed package. The estimated value is not a verified final contract price.

The claim will need reassessment when an accessible official notification, final agreement, contract or delivery record supplies material new evidence. The broad inference about regional policy is analysis; the testable factual question here is what was approved and what, if anything, was subsequently contracted or delivered.

Military Times links the August 31 State Department notification, and Deagel reproduces its text. Direct retrieval of the official page returned HTTP 403, so this review does not claim to have read the live official original.
